councilSetup.title: Configure the AI team
councilSetup.description: Confirm the hard requirements, then choose models, roles and session rules for this council.

example.name: Repository analysis SaaS
example.idea: Design the best architecture for a SaaS platform that analyzes GitHub repositories, finds security and quality problems and automatically proposes code improvements as pull requests.
example.goal: A production-ready MVP within three months that a team of three can operate.
example.requirements: EU data residency. Private repositories must never be used for model training. Budget for infrastructure below 1,000 EUR per month at launch.

projectForm.restored: Your unsaved draft from this browser was restored.
projectForm.name: Project name
projectForm.repositoryHint: If GitHub is connected and covers this repository, it is linked automatically; otherwise link it on the project page.
projectForm.ideaHint: Every AI model receives exactly this brief during Independent Thinking.
projectForm.ideaTooShort: Describe the idea in at least 20 characters
projectForm.intentHint: Development starts only after you approve a decision.
projectForm.goalHint: What does a good result look like?
projectForm.requirementsHint: Constraints such as budget, compliance or tech stack.

documents.formats: PDF, Word (.docx) and PowerPoint (.pptx) up to 8 MB, images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) up to 3.5 MB, text files up to 200 kB; at most 10 per project. From PDF, Word and PowerPoint only the text is read. An image is described in text first – by an AI model of your choice or by you – and you confirm the description; the council reads only that text.
documents.imageIntro: The council reads this image only as text. Let a model describe it (one call on your own key, usually under 1 cent) or write the description yourself, check it and confirm it.
documents.descriptionBy: Description (draft by {model} – check and correct it)

repoLink.none: No repository linked. The Execution Council will start from an empty workspace.
repoLink.notLinked: The brief names {url}, but it is not linked: the CONSYRIUM AI GitHub App probably has no access to it. On GitHub open Settings → Applications → the CONSYRIUM AI app → Configure, add the repository, then click “Load repositories” and link it here. Without a link no pull request can be created.
repoLink.notConfigured: GitHub is not configured on this server.
repoLink.notInPlan: GitHub is not included in your plan. <link>See Billing & usage</link>.

repoContext.saved: Saved. Confirm the requirements again before the next council – the sources changed.
repoContext.saveError: Could not save the repository context
repoContext.intro: The models of a Decision council read the files you choose here, frozen at one commit, as context – not as requirements. Every model call reads them, so they add to the token use of a council.
repoContext.readable: {n, plural, one {# readable text file} other {# readable text files}}
repoContext.size: {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}, {size} ≈ {tokens} tokens per model call
repoContext.savedState: Saved: {repo} @ {sha} · {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} · {size} · ≈ {tokens} tokens per model call
repoContext.removed: Repository context removed. Confirm the requirements again before the next council.
repoContext.removeError: The repository context could not be removed
repoContext.removeConfirm: Remove the repository context? The models then no longer read these files, and the requirements must be confirmed again.
repoContext.newerCommit: The branch has moved on since the saved state ({saved} → {current}). Your saved selection is kept; save to update the context to the new commit.
repoContext.saveConfirm: Save these files as context? The requirements must then be confirmed again before the next council, because the sources change.

suspicion.instruction: Reads like an instruction to the AI models (e.g. to ignore rules or to rate a proposal). The models never follow it.
suspicion.quoted_instruction: Quotes text that reads like an instruction to the AI models. If the product must handle this text as data (store, show, filter it), keep it – the models check it as a requirement and never follow the quoted text.
suspicion.meta_rule: Says when a requirement counts as met instead of describing the product. The council judges every proposal on substance; keep it only if it is a real product rule.

requirements.title: Hard requirements
requirements.intro: The council checks every proposal against exactly this list. Review it before the start – the number of sentences in the brief is no proof that nothing is missing.
requirements.changed: The brief or its documents changed after version {version} was confirmed (brief version {briefVersion}). Review the list and confirm it again before starting a council. Councils that already run keep the list they were started with.
requirements.confirmedNone: Confirmed: this brief has no hard requirements.
requirements.severalLimits: several limits – not checked as numbers
requirements.splitLimits: several limits in one sentence – split it to check each as a number
requirements.excludedSummary: {n, plural, one {# statement deliberately not taken over} other {# statements deliberately not taken over}}
requirements.sourceGone: source no longer in the brief
requirements.toDecideText: Nothing is kept or removed here on its own. Decide each statement before you confirm; the original wording stays unchanged.
requirements.excludedText: These statements from the brief or a document are not binding. Give a reason for each; they are shown to the council as excluded, so they do not come back as requirements.
requirements.reasonLabel: Reason for not taking it over
requirements.pendingImages: Confirm the description of {names} on the project page first – the council reads an image only through its confirmed description, so the requirements cannot be confirmed before.
requirements.unscanned: Not scanned for requirements (format): {names}. Add their hard requirements by hand.
requirements.notProposed: {n, plural, one {# further statement was not proposed because the list is full. Add it by hand if it is a requirement.} other {# further statements were not proposed because the list is full. Add the ones that are requirements by hand.}}
requirements.noHard: This brief has no hard requirements.
requirements.readOnly: Only members who can edit the project can confirm the requirements.
requirements.afterImplementationText: Before anything is built, no model can confirm “{text}”, so the council will end with “needs verification”. Keep it as it is, and add how it is measured (method, target value) so the proposals can be compared on it.
requirements.addPlan: Add a measurement plan as a requirement

reasons.injection: Reads like an instruction to the AI models, not a product requirement
reasons.metaRule: Says when a requirement counts as met instead of describing the product – the council judges proposals on substance
reasons.context: From the idea or goal – context, not a hard requirement. Keep it if it is one.
reasons.document: From a document, without binding wording (must, only, at most, a limit …) – a description, table row or measured value. Keep it if it is a requirement.
reasons.instruction: A work instruction to the council for this run, not a product requirement. Keep it if it is one.
reasons.duplicate: Repeats a requirement from the requirements field, so it is listed once. Keep it if it says more.

requirements.undecidedError: At least one proposed statement is neither kept nor excluded with a reason. Reload the page and decide every marked statement.
requirements.conflict: {first} and {second} may contradict each other: deletion within {deleteDays} days, but retention for at least {retainDays} days. No proposal can meet both – change one of them before you start the council.
requirements.reasonMissingError: At least one statement you did not take over has no reason (at least 3 characters). Add it and confirm again.
requirements.buildCheckHint: Only the implementation can prove this (tests, CI). The council checks that a proposal names a concrete verification plan; the build verifies it.

split.proposalNote: Each part keeps its wording, numbers and negations and refers to the original. Nothing is split unless you choose to.
split.coupled: Conditions that belong together – checked as one requirement.

unclear.alternatives: Contains alternatives (or) – splitting could change the meaning. Split it yourself if the parts are independent.
unclear.shared_scope: A word at the start may apply to every item (e.g. “must”, “no”, “only”) – split it yourself if the parts are independent.
unclear.coverage: A split would lose a number or negation – split it yourself if the parts are independent.

split.limit: This would exceed 100 requirements per list – remove or merge requirements first.
split.gaps: The original contains {tokens}, but no part does – check the parts so nothing gets lost.

checkability.summary: {before} checkable before the start · {after} measurable only after implementation · {build} checked in the build

voteWeights.title: Vote weights
voteWeights.intro: How much each model's scores and ranking count in the Final Verdict. Its own proposal is never weighted, and the feasibility check counts every model once. Fixed when the council starts.
voteWeights.sourceNote: Suggestions from the <link>{source}</link> (percentile tier 1–10). A model that is not in the ranking gets the neutral 5.

warning.dominant: {model} holds {share} % of the vote and outweighs all other models together.
warning.dominantTwo: {model} holds {share} % of the vote – at least twice the weight of {other}, so its evaluation mostly sets the ranking.

mode.title: 2. Decision mode
mode.independent_expert: Blind expert proposals with lighter structured feedback. Architecture, strategy, technology choice.
mode.adversarial_review: Deep 12 Minds scrutiny, rebuttals, two independent judges per objection. Security and high-stakes decisions.
mode.consensus: Several revision passes and an optional hybrid proposal. Dissent stays documented.

problem.plan: Your {plan} plan allows up to {n} models per session.
problem.roles: Activate at least one 12 Minds Council role.
problem.weights: Fix the highlighted Final Verdict weights (each 0–100).
problem.budgetTooSmall: The budget is too small for this team: at least {tokens} tokens are needed so every model can write a proposal and the Final Verdict can still run.
problem.open: {n, plural, one {1 thing left before you can start:} other {# things left before you can start:}}

models.title: 1. Select AI models
models.intro: Loaded live from your providers. Choose {min}–{max} models; different providers give more independent views.
models.introPlan: Loaded live from your providers. Choose {min}–{max} models (limit of your {plan} plan); different providers give more independent views.
models.noKeys: No API keys yet. <link>Add a provider key</link> first.
models.unavailableHint: The last call of this model in this workspace was refused by the provider (model not found). It stays selectable: every council start checks it again, and the note disappears as soon as the model answers or after 24 hours.

roles.addedTitle: {n, plural, one {One model} other {# models}} had no perspective – added automatically, so every model gives its own critical review (still one vote per model):
roles.addedToggle: Extra perspectives for {n, plural, one {the model} other {the # models}} without a role
roles.addedCost: {calls, plural, one {# extra model call} other {# extra model calls}} in the 12 Minds Council (already in the cost estimate). Two perspectives of one model are not two independent opinions – every model keeps one vote.
roles.addedOff: Off: {n, plural, one {one model gives} other {# models give}} no own critical review in the 12 Minds Council.
roles.title: 3. 12 Minds Council perspectives
roles.intro: {n} active. Perspectives are not independent votes: majorities are counted per model. Fewer roles cost less.
roles.vsModels: {models, plural, one {# model} other {# models}} · {perspectives, plural, one {# perspective} other {# perspectives}} · each proposal is checked by up to {foreign, plural, one {# other model} other {# other models}} (if all of them keep answering). Perspectives are not votes: several roles on one model stay one model.
roles.instances: {model}: {n} instances (different keys) count as 1 independent voice – for majorities, the minimum of two independent reviewers and cross-checks. An instance never reviews another instance of its model.

purpose.title: What is this council for?
purpose.ideaHint: You are at the start and want to know whether the idea holds up. Result: a favourite, the variants ruled out and a list of what to clarify before the next step.
purpose.approvalHint: You want to have it built afterwards. Result: approval only when every evaluator confirmed every requirement.
purpose.note: Process, cost and checks are equally strict for both – only the way the result is presented differs.

settings.title: 4. Session settings
settings.hybrid: Allow a hybrid proposal (reviewed like any other)
settings.budgetHint: {min}–{max} tokens. Calls stop when the budget would be exceeded. Providers bill your own keys.
settings.rulesHint: E.g. “Focus on operating cost” or “Must run in the EU”.
settings.budgetNeeds: Needs at least {needed} tokens – set to {set}.
settings.budgetFewer: Even the highest budget is not enough for this team – choose fewer models or roles.
settings.budgetAdjusted: Budget adjusted: {from} → {to} tokens. You can still change the value.

summary.title: Before you start
summary.estimate: About {calls} model calls in total, at most {tokens} tokens (upper bound).
summary.estimateDocs: About {calls} model calls in total, at most {tokens} tokens (upper bound), including {docs, plural, one {# attached document} other {# attached documents}}.
summary.typical: Typically about {tokens} tokens (median of your last {calls} calls).
summary.noTypical: No typical value yet: too few earlier calls in this workspace.
summary.splitVerdict: Too large for one evaluation: each model checks the requirements in {calls} calls of at most {perCall}. The brief and proposals are sent once per call – the estimate and the budget include this.
summary.twoModels: With two models each proposal has only one independent evaluator: this council can name a provisional favourite, but never a recommendation you can approve. Choose three or more models for a recommendation.
summary.contextDoesNotFit: {model}: the brief, documents and all proposals need about {input} tokens, its context window has {window}. Its calls would be refused rather than cut off – choose a model with a larger window or a smaller repository context.
summary.overBudget: The upper bound exceeds your budget of {budget} tokens. I accept that debate phases may be shortened to keep enough budget for the Final Verdict: if the budget runs short, Minority Review and Consensus Round are dropped and the proposals are not revised – the verdict then judges the first versions and is marked as shortened.
summary.checkWeights: Check the vote weights before you start:
summary.typicalRange: Typically about {low}–{high} tokens (from your last {calls} calls).
summary.belowTypical: Your budget of {budget} tokens is below what such a council typically needs (up to about {high}). Debate phases will then likely be shortened and the verdict marked as shortened.

catalog.metaDescription: Reviewed community skills for CONSYRIUM AI councils: perspectives, requirement building blocks, weights and rules.
catalog.title: SkillHub
catalog.intro: Decision packages for CONSYRIUM AI councils. Community skills are checked automatically and approved by an admin before they are published; official skills (@consyrium) come from CONSYRIUM AI. A skill only pre-fills a council – you confirm the requirements and approve as usual.

detail.licenseText: Published under {license} by @{handle}. Using it creates your own copy that names the original.
detail.uses: {n, plural, =0 {not adopted yet} one {adopted by # workspace} other {adopted by # workspaces}}

skillHub.disclaimer: Community skill – not legal, medical or financial advice and no guarantee by CONSYRIUM AI. A skill never changes the requirement gate, the reviews or the human approval.

actions.adoptHint: Creates your own private copy in your workspace (sign-in required).
actions.reportHint: Reports go to the admins. They never hide a skill automatically.
actions.reported: Thank you – the admins will look at it.
actions.alreadyAdopted: Already in your skills – no second copy created.
actions.adoptedProfile: Adopted – a private copy is now in your role profiles and can be chosen for its role in the council setup.
actions.adoptProfileHint: Creates a private copy with its origin (CC BY 4.0, author named). It does not update itself.

footer.license: Community skills are published under CC BY 4.0 by their authors (shown as @handle). No legal, financial or medical advice.

profile.sourcesHint: Named by the author – not checked by CONSYRIUM AI. Links are shown as text.
profile.notice: Written by another user and published under CC BY 4.0 after review. It only sharpens what its role looks at; it cannot change requirements, votes, weights or the approval. It may not imitate real people.
